newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Canada's Inco eyes nickel demand in '98.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Inco eyes nickel demand in '98.

text.p: Canada-based nickel producer Inco Ltd sees demand for nickel outstripping supply next year thanks to increased stainless steel production, especially in Asia, a company executive said on Tuesday.

"In 1998 demand will exceed supply, giving a positive impact to nickel prices," Inco executive vice-president Peter Goudie told reporters after the annual shareholders' meeting of Inco subsidiary PT International Nickel Indonesia.
Inco Ltd has a 58.73 percent stake in PT Inco, Sumitomo Metal Mining Co Ltd has 20.09 percent, private shareholders 20 percent and the rest is held by four Japanese companies.
Goudie said demand and supply were expected to be "roughly balanced" this year compared with surplus supply last year because of a decline in stainless steel production.

Nickel, whose two best-known uses are in nickel coinage and nickel plating, is widely used in the production of stainless steel, which accounts for nearly two-thirds of total annual nickel consumption.
"If we look into 1998, we will continue to see an increase in demand. Demand is going to continue to grow faster in Asia. When I say Asia, I am talking about Asia outside Japan.
"Because of the expected increase in stainless steel production in Taiwan and South Korea ... that should generate a significant increase in nickel demand," Goudie told Reuters.
He said Asian countries had until recently been significant importers of stainless steel and that their markets could expand stainless steel production and rely less on imports.
"And that has enabled them over the past few years to have quite a strong increase in stainless steel production because they have been such large net importers," he added.

Meanwhile, PT Inco vice-president and chief financial officer Ray Westall said the company was expected to produce 92 million pounds of nickel-in-matte this year, up from 87.1 million pounds last year.

He told Reuters that one of the three furnaces at the company's Soroako plant on Sulawesi island had been shut down since January 26 for maintenance and was scheduled to resume operations in mid-July.
"The number one furnace is down for maintenance. It's been on line for 10 years, so we are taking it down for repairs," he said. "It will start again in mid-July."

PT Inco president and chief executive, Rumengan Musu, said in a statement issued after the shareholders' meeting that the company's capital expenditure was expected to total some $289 million this year, up from $178 million in 1996.

He said some $245 million would go towards the company's expansion plan to raise the annual production capacity to 150 million pounds of nickel from 100 million. Initial production from the expanded facilities are to begin by the end of 1998.
